answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. What survives to the falcon is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. A walnut of per-task receipts records who did what, and the jetty of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. The design leans on staked peer review with spot checks, published publicly on failure, every claim is re-checked by someone with nothing to gain.
